title: United Provinces of New Granada
capsule: The United Provinces of New Granada was a short-lived confederal republic formed in 1811 during the Primera República phase of New Granadan independence, when several provinces including Cartagena, Antioquia, and Tunja declared autonomy from Spain and signed a federal compact following the dissolution of viceregal authority in 1810. The confederation was fractured by the simultaneous existence of a rival centralist state centred on Bogotá (Cundinamarca), and the two factions fought intermittently in what patriots called La Patria Boba ('the Foolish Fatherland'). Spanish reconquest forces under Pablo Morillo arrived in 1815 and suppressed both the confederal and centralist republics by 1816, reimposing royalist rule until Simón Bolívar's liberation campaign of 1819.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The jurisdictional boundaries of the constituent provinces are reasonably well documented from Spanish colonial administrative records, but effective territorial control was fragmented and contested throughout this period.
